mainEntity.name: Do you do the inside as well?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We are exterior only and we quote that way so the scopes do not overlap with your internal cleaner. Most builders already have one, and keeping the boundary clean is what stops things being double paid for or assumed to be the other party.

mainEntity.name: How far before handover should it be done?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Three to five days. Close enough that it still presents when the buyer walks through, far enough out that there is room to come back if a trade marks a surface afterwards.

Cleaning three weeks early looks efficient on a programme and almost always means doing it twice.

mainEntity.name: Can you remove concrete slurry from a brand new driveway?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, and it is better done soon. Fresh slurry comes off a new slab easily. Cured through a summer it needs acid, and acid on green concrete carries a real risk of etching because the surface has not hardened.

We test the strength on a small area out of sight first, and on a very fresh pour the honest answer is sometimes to wait a few weeks.

mainEntity.name: What if a trade marks something after you have been?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Within a reasonable window before handover we come back and deal with it. It is a build site and that is normal.

What we will not do is clean a lot well ahead of schedule and then treat the inevitable damage as a new job. Timing the clean properly is what avoids the argument.

mainEntity.name: Do you price per lot on an estate?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, by dwelling type, so the exterior clean sits in the build cost rather than appearing as a variable at the end. Lots are sequenced against your handover dates rather than done in a batch.

One contact, one account, one invoice, whether it is three townhouses or thirty lots.

mainEntity.name: Will you provide insurance and site documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whatever your site requires, before the first attendance. Tell us what is needed at quote stage and it will be in place rather than being sorted out at the gate.
